description: Convert a broad factual record into a compact issue-specific record by linking only legally material facts to the governing elements and the assigned burden.
application_scenario: Use when a case contains a lengthy chronology or many background facts but each issue turns on a narrower set of facts.
reasoning_flow: State the precise legal issue without embedding the requested disposition.
Identify the governing rule, test, or doctrinal elements and note which party bears each burden.
Sort the record into facts material to each element, facts relevant only to another issue, and background facts.
Separate facts tending in different directions and identify material evidentiary gaps.
Apply the filtered facts element by element and record an issue-level determination for later composition.
example_application: In a dispute with an extensive history of dealings, isolate the communications and conduct bearing on the disputed obligation, map them to formation and performance elements, and leave unrelated background events outside that issue analysis.

description: Sequence dependent issues so that liability or entitlement is assessed before remedial eligibility and the amount or form of relief.
application_scenario: Use when a claim presents separate questions about breach, fault, status, or entitlement and then asks what relief or compensation follows.
reasoning_flow: Identify the threshold merits issue that must be resolved before any remedy is considered.
Evaluate each required merits element and any complete or partial defense.
Determine which categories of relief become legally available under the merits determination.
Assess causation, remoteness, mitigation, and proof requirements for each available category.
Calculate or structure the remedy by separate heads and combine the issue-level determinations without double counting.
example_application: For an employment dispute, first assess whether termination breached the governing obligations, then identify compensable loss categories, examine mitigation evidence, and calculate each category separately.

description: Resolve disputes in which the same transfer, payment, or arrangement is assigned competing legal meanings by the parties.
application_scenario: Use when one side characterizes a transaction as a loan, purchase, trust, partnership contribution, agency arrangement, or other legal relationship and the opposing side advances a different characterization.
reasoning_flow: List the competing legal characterizations and the consequences attached to each.
Identify objective indicators such as documents, payment routing, control, possession, repayment terms, and subsequent conduct.
Distinguish contemporaneous evidence from later explanations created after the dispute arose.
Test each characterization against the full course of dealing and applicable presumptions.
Select the characterization that best accounts for the material evidence, then pass that classification to the relevant liability or remedy template.
example_application: Where money was transferred and later claimed back, compare whether the record better reflects a repayable advance, an investment contribution, or property held for another, using contemporaneous communications and control over the funds.

description: Determine which version of a legal rule applies and whether later repeal, amendment, limitation, or changed circumstances affect an earlier transaction or status.
application_scenario: Use when rights arose under an earlier legal regime, a provision later changed, a limitation period is invoked, or the governing test requires assessment at a particular time.
reasoning_flow: Build a chronology of the legally significant event, accrual of the asserted right, commencement of proceedings, and any relevant legal change.
Identify the default rules on prospectivity, retrospectivity, savings, accrued rights, and limitation.
Determine the legally prescribed assessment date for the issue.
Apply the rule in force at that assessment point while accounting for any transitional or saving provision.
State separately the effect of elapsed time, legal change, and later factual developments.
example_application: For a claim based on a family status formed under an earlier regime, identify when the asserted status and inheritance interest arose, then examine whether a later statutory change altered accrued rights or only future cases.

description: Evaluate whether a disputed document, product, shipment, or other item is genuine and connected to the alleged source through a traceable evidentiary chain.
application_scenario: Use when the merits depend on authorship, manufacture, shipment, execution, custody, loss of an original, or another contested source relationship.
reasoning_flow: Define the specific proposition of authenticity, origin, or custody that must be proved.
Identify the party bearing the burden and the applicable standard of proof.
Construct the chain from creation or dispatch through custody, transfer, receipt, and present production.
Assess direct evidence, records, physical or technical indicators, and witness reliability at each link.
Examine alternative sources, breaks in custody, missing originals, and whether any inference or presumption arises.
Record the provenance finding and pass it to the substantive infringement, probate, carriage, or contract analysis.
example_application: When goods are alleged to come from a particular manufacturer, trace purchase and distribution records, compare product features and witness evidence, and test the counterfeiting alternative before addressing infringement.

description: Resolve a procedural threshold that controls whether, where, or in what form the substantive dispute may proceed.
application_scenario: Use for appeals, amendments to a costs bill, consolidation, summary processes, winding-up petitions, or other matters requiring a gateway determination before full merits review.
reasoning_flow: Identify the procedural order sought and the legal threshold governing that order.
Separate the gateway question from the underlying substantive controversy.
Determine whether the applicant has supplied the minimum evidentiary and procedural foundation.
Assess prejudice, duplication, efficiency, finality, and availability of an ordinary trial or alternative procedure where relevant.
Define the permitted scope of further adjudication after the gateway determination.
example_application: In a summary debt-based proceeding, first ask whether the debtor has shown a genuine dispute grounded in substantial evidence; only if the gateway permits should the process move to the requested corporate remedy.

description: Assess whether a claimant who has crossed the merits threshold should receive a discretionary remedy and on what terms.
application_scenario: Use for interim or final injunctions, declarations, validation terms, enforcement orders, buy-out relief, or comparable remedies not granted automatically upon proof of a right.
reasoning_flow: Confirm the legal and evidentiary threshold for considering the requested remedy.
Identify the practical harm to each side if the remedy is imposed or withheld.
Assess adequacy of damages, preservation of the subject matter, urgency, delay, conduct, and enforceability.
Consider effects on third parties and whether narrower terms can reduce unnecessary prejudice.
Formulate proportionate conditions, duration, scope, or safeguards for the remedy.
example_application: For continuation of an asset-preservation order, evaluate the strength of the underlying claim, risk to the assets, hardship to the respondent, adequacy of other relief, and whether tailored exceptions can protect ordinary dealings.

description: Evaluate a corporate restructuring or insolvency-related request by testing statutory purpose, financial justification, and protection of creditors and other affected stakeholders.
application_scenario: Use for capital reductions, validation orders, winding-up-related terms, rectification, or similar corporate applications affecting the company's asset pool or stakeholder rights.
reasoning_flow: Identify the corporate act requested and the statutory conditions attached to it.
Examine the commercial purpose and whether the proposed act is connected to a legitimate corporate need.
Assess the company's financial position and the effect on the asset pool available to creditors.
Identify creditor notice, consent, security, solvency evidence, and other protective measures.
Check effects on members and third parties, including equality of treatment and procedural regularity.
Specify any safeguards or terms needed to align the corporate act with stakeholder protection.
example_application: For a proposed reduction of capital, examine whether the capital exceeds operational needs, whether the proposal serves a discernible purpose, and whether creditors remain protected through solvency evidence or other safeguards.

description: Analyze an accident by separating breach of duty, factual causation, legal causation, and any contribution by the claimant.
application_scenario: Use in personal injury, road accident, workplace injury, property damage, or nuisance-related cases where multiple acts may have produced the harm.
reasoning_flow: Define the relevant duties and the concrete precautions reasonably required in the circumstances.
Reconstruct the event using location, timing, movement, visibility, warnings, control, and physical-contact evidence.
Determine whether each alleged breach materially contributed to the injury or loss.
Test alternative causal explanations and distinguish the mechanism of contact from the ultimate injury.
Assess whether the claimant's conduct contributed to the harm and, if so, the relative causal responsibility.
Pass the resulting fault allocation to the damages assessment.
example_application: In a pedestrian accident, evaluate vehicle positioning, speed, lookout, warnings, and the pedestrian's own movement, then distinguish whether injury followed from direct contact or an intervening object.

description: Assess compensation through separate, non-overlapping heads of loss using evidence appropriate to past, future, pecuniary, and non-pecuniary harm.
application_scenario: Use after liability or statutory entitlement is established in personal injury, fatal accident, employment, trespass, nuisance, or commercial loss disputes.
reasoning_flow: Identify each legally recoverable head of loss and exclude categories outside the pleaded or statutory basis.
Separate past losses from future losses and pecuniary losses from non-pecuniary harm.
Evaluate medical, employment, financial, valuation, and dependency evidence relevant to each head.
Apply causation, remoteness, mitigation, contingencies, and any statutory limits.
Check for overlap among loss categories and adjust for payments or benefits that must be credited.
Aggregate the independently assessed heads into a transparent compensation structure.
example_application: For an injury claim, assess pain and loss of amenities separately from past earnings, future earning capacity, care costs, and expenses, using medical and employment evidence for each category.

template_name: Legal Recognition of Personal or Family Status
description: Determine whether a personal or family relationship receives legal recognition and what succession, probate, or matrimonial consequences follow.
application_scenario: Use when a claim depends on being recognized as a child, adopted child, spouse, beneficiary, or other legally significant family relation.
reasoning_flow: Identify the precise status asserted and the legal consequence for which recognition is sought.
Determine the formal, customary, statutory, or evidentiary requirements for that status.
Examine the relationship's formation, public treatment, household conduct, documentary record, and any competing status claims.
Address temporal changes in recognition rules and any presumptions arising from missing or informal documentation.
Separate the status finding from later questions concerning succession, validity of a testamentary instrument, marital breakdown, or costs.
example_application: Where individuals claim succession rights through a parent-child relationship formed under customary practices, assess the legal recognition requirements and evidence of the relationship before considering entitlement to the estate.

description: Determine whether a commercial document or mode of performance satisfies the governing contractual or rule-based requirements and produces the asserted legal effect.
application_scenario: Use when payment, delivery, transfer, sale, mortgage, or credit obligations depend on the form, contents, presentation, or legal effect of documents.
reasoning_flow: Identify the operative instrument and the exact documentary or performance conditions.
Separate facial compliance of the document from the truth of the underlying transaction unless the governing regime links them.
Compare each required field, signature, description, timing condition, and presentation step with the submitted material.
Assess waiver, variation, course of dealing, substitution, and any discrepancy claimed by the opposing party.
Determine the legal consequence of each material discrepancy and pass that determination to the payment, ownership, or enforcement analysis.
example_application: For a documentary payment dispute, compare the presented transport record with the instrument's stated requirements, distinguish document examination from the underlying shipment, and assess whether any discrepancy was waived.
